title: The Hidden Risks of Child Interpreters in Care
summary: Learn why using child interpreters in healthcare can affect accuracy, privacy, patient voice, and family roles.
body_markdown:
###


Children should not be used as the routine medical interpreter. HHS guidance strongly limits reliance on accompanying minors and encourages covered entities to provide competent language assistance.


###


A child may omit details, simplify medical language, answer for the parent, hear sensitive information, or change what the patient feels comfortable saying.


###


Thank the family, explain that professional language support is available, start the interpreter, and repeat any clinically important information that was discussed before professional interpretation began.


###


Yes. Family members can support the patient, provide collateral history, or participate in decisions when the patient wants them involved without serving as the main language channel.


###


Yes. Immediate AI medical interpretation can give staff a professional language option before a child becomes the default interpreter, especially during short or unscheduled interactions.
